Bodrum is often called the St. Tropez of Turkey, and one look at the whitewashed streets and swanky beach clubs will tell you why. But don’t write it off if you’re not a champagne-on-the-sundeck type. There’s a lot more to Bodrum than fancy hotels and pricey cocktails!

With a medieval castle, tons of amazing food, and the Aegean right on your doorstep, Bodrum has a lot to offer. The only question is: where do you start?

Well, that’s where we come in! We’ve pulled together ten of the best things to do in Bodrum, with practical tips and all of the need-to-know info along the way.

Bodrum At A Glance

Bodrum is a beautiful coastal city on Turkey’s Aegean coast. It’s often referred to as the St. Tropez of Turkey, although the whitewashed buildings and windmills actually remind us more of Mykonos or Santorini. If you’re looking for gorgeous beaches and glamorous resorts, you’re bound to fall in love with this dreamy destination.

Important Tip: Don’t rely on taxis to get around Bodrum, as they can get pretty expensive! While the town itself is very walkable, we recommend renting a car or hopping on the local dolmuş minibusses if you want to explore the wider peninsula without blowing your budget.

How long to stay: We recommend spending at least three days in Bodrum to explore the main attractions. But trust us, you could easily stay longer if you want more beach time.

Budget accordingly: Bodrum is generally more expensive than other destinations in Turkey, especially around the luxury resort areas. However, you can save money by staying in the main town and visiting during the shoulder season. May, June, September, and October are great options if you want to avoid the peak summer prices and crowds.

Explore beyond Bodrum town: Some of the prettiest spots are scattered around the Bodrum Peninsula, so don’t spend your entire trip in the city center! Gümüşlük is fantastic for waterfront seafood restaurants and sunsets, Yalıkavak is known for its glamorous marina, and Bitez is a great spot for a relaxing beach day.

How We Would Spend Three Days in Bodrum

🏰 Day 1: Historic Sights & Seaside Villages
Explore Bodrum’s historic sights on a private city tour, then spend the afternoon and evening in the fishing village of Gümüşlük.

🍴 Day 2: Turkish Cooking, Old Town & Marina
Visit a local farmers’ market and learn to prepare Turkish food with this fantastic cooking class, then explore Bodrum’s Old Town and marina.

⛵ Day 3: Coastal Cruise, Sunset & Nightlife
Cruise along the coast on a traditional gulet and watch the sunset from the Bodrum Windmills, then enjoy the city’s nightlife (as long as your flight out isn’t too early!). 

Love the sound of this trip? We’ve mapped it all out in our full 3-day Bodrum itinerary here!

Things to do in Bodrum

1. Learn how to cook Turkish food and visit a farmers’ market

Tour Details

  • Duration: 6 hours
  • Time: 9:30 am
  • Highlights: Visiting a local farmers’ market, preparing traditional Turkish mezes and other dishes, enjoying a homemade meal
  • Inclusions: Local host and cooking instructor, ingredients, lunch, water, tea, coffee, alcoholic beverages, transportation from selected pickup areas, small group tour
  • Rating: 4.8 stars (check 70+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

We absolutely LOVE Turkish food, so naturally, we couldn’t resist booking this traditional cooking class while we were in Bodrum. And we’re so glad we did, because it turned out to be one of our favorite experiences!

The day started with a visit to a local farmers’ market, where our host helped us pick out fresh ingredients for our cooking class. We loved exploring the stalls and learning about all of the local produce. Plus, it was fun shopping alongside the locals rather than just browsing for the same old souvenirs.

Then it was time to get cooking. We learned how to prepare a selection of traditional Aegean-Turkish dishes, including five different mezes, a pastry starter, and a main course. The menu changes depending on what’s in season, so everything was super fresh.

Our host was fantastic at explaining the different ingredients and techniques, and we picked up some really useful tips along the way. But of course, the best part was sitting down to eat everything we’d made. We got to enjoy all of the food al fresco in the hosts’ gorgeous garden, which was such a treat, and we washed it down with some local wine – life really doesn’t get much better.

There were only six people in our group, so the whole experience felt really personal, and we had plenty of opportunities to ask questions. We had such a fun time, and let’s just say we definitely didn’t leave hungry!

Book this awesome Turkish cooking class here! 

2. See Bodrum’s top city sites 

Tour Details

  • Duration: 4–5 hours
  • Time: Flexible departure times, arranged around your cruise schedule
  • Highlights: Exploring Bodrum Castle and the Underwater Archaeology Museum, visiting Myndos Gate, the windmills, Ancient Theatre, and Bodrum Bazaar
  • Inclusions: Private licensed guide, air-conditioned vehicle and driver, cruise port pickup and drop-off, parking fees (castle and museum admission extra)
  • Rating: 4.9 stars (check 250+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

Bodrum has a fascinating history, and there’s a LOT more to see here than beautiful beaches and expensive yachts! We think this private sightseeing tour is the best way to discover the city’s most important landmarks, especially if you’re visiting on a cruise.

The tour starts with Bodrum Castle, an enormous medieval fortress built by the Knights of St. John in the 15th century. It’s one of the city’s most impressive buildings, and the views from the castle are fantastic.

Inside, you’ll also visit the Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology, which houses fascinating artifacts recovered from ancient shipwrecks. We think this is a fascinating museum, especially since the Aegean has been an important trading route for thousands of years.

But there’s plenty more to see! You’ll also visit the ancient Myndos Gate, the ruins of Bodrum’s old windmills, and the Ancient Theatre, which dates back to the 4th century BC. It’s amazing to think people gathered here to watch performances more than 2,000 years ago. The tour also includes time at Bodrum Bazaar, where you can browse the shops and pick up a few souvenirs. 

One thing we especially like is that you’ll have a private guide and driver, so you won’t have to worry about navigating the city yourself. The itinerary is flexible, too, which means you can spend more time at the places that interest you most.

3. Explore the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus

Did you know that Bodrum was once home to one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World? The Mausoleum of Halicarnassus was an enormous tomb built for Mausolus, the ruler of Caria, in the 4th century BC, and it’s one of the city’s most fascinating historical sites.

Now, we should probably mention that the original mausoleum isn’t still standing. It was damaged over the centuries, and today you’ll find its foundations and surviving architectural fragments rather than an enormous ancient monument.

But we still think it’s worth visiting, especially if you’re interested in history! Information panels and displays help you imagine what the original building looked like. We find it pretty incredible that this site was once considered one of the most spectacular buildings in the ancient world.

In fact, the mausoleum was so famous that its name eventually became the word we use for grand tombs today. How’s that for a lasting legacy?

The archaeological site is close to central Bodrum, so you can easily fit it into a morning of sightseeing without traveling far. We allow around 45 minutes to explore, though you can spend longer if you enjoy reading about ancient history. It’s also worth combining this with Bodrum Castle and the Ancient Theatre if you’re keen to discover more about the city’s past.

4. Enjoy a private luxury gulet cruise

Tour Details

  • Duration: 1–7 hours
  • Time: Flexible departure times
  • Highlights: Private luxury gulet cruise, visiting secluded bays, swimming and snorkeling along the Aegean coastline
  • Inclusions: Private boat and crew, Turkish lunch, bottled water, tea and coffee (other drinks extra)
  • Rating: 4.9 stars (check 160+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

If there’s one thing we’d recommend splashing out on in Bodrum, it’s a boat trip! The coastline around the peninsula is absolutely gorgeous, and we think this private luxury gulet cruise sounds like an amazing way to explore it.

If you’re not familiar with gulets, they’re traditional Turkish wooden sailing boats, and they’re a big part of the experience when visiting this part of Turkey. With spacious decks and plenty of places to stretch out in the sunshine, they’re perfect for a relaxing day on the water.

On this tour, you’ll have the entire boat to yourselves, so you won’t have to share with strangers or compete for the best sunbed! You’ll cruise along the beautiful Aegean coastline, stopping at several secluded bays where you can jump into the sea for a swim or try some snorkeling. The itinerary usually includes four or five different swimming spots, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to cool off.

There’s also a freshly prepared Turkish lunch served on board, which sounds like a pretty fantastic way to refuel between swims. Just be aware that drinks are paid for separately.

We especially like that you can choose your preferred departure time and spend the day at your own pace. Whether you fancy spending most of your time swimming or simply relaxing on deck, it’s entirely up to you!

Ready for a day on the water? Book your private gulet cruise here!

Alternate option: Shared cruise

If you’re traveling solo or don’t fancy paying for a private charter, this shared boat trip is a much more wallet-friendly alternative. It’s a six-hour cruise that takes you to Bodrum’s best swimming spots, including Black Island, Poyraz Bay and Rabbit Bay, with plenty of time to enjoy each one. Lunch is thrown in too, and there’s a bar on board, which is always a win! 

We think that this is perfect if you want to spend a dreamy day out on the water without hiring an entire boat. This is a very popular one, though, so we would recommend taking advantage of Viator’s free cancellation policy and locking in your dates  ASAP.

5. Visit Gümüşlük

If you’ve had your fill of glitz and glam and want a more down-to-earth day, head to Gümüşlük. It’s a little fishing village on the western side of the peninsula, and it’s about a 30-minute drive from Bodrum town, but it feels like a whole different world!

Gümüşlük has definitely gotten busier in recent years, but it’s still far more laid-back than Bodrum’s swanky resort areas. A wander along the waterfront and a nosy at the shops is about as busy as your afternoon needs to get.

The real reason to come here, though, is the food. Gümüşlük is famous for its seafood restaurants, and it’s hard to beat a plate of freshly caught fish and crisp white wine right by the water.

If you want somewhere with a view, we loved Limon, which sits up on a hillside above the sea and is known for its sunsets. Just be sure to book ahead if you want a table! Or if you’d prefer to stay down on the waterfront, Karafaki Erhan Usta is another fantastic spot for fresh seafood and views over the bay.

Not hungry yet? You can lounge on the beach and then hop on a boat trip, or visit the open-air market if it’s on. You don’t need a tour to visit this place, either. It’s easy to get here via a local dolmuş from Bodrum, or of course you can drive yourself if you’ve got a rental car. 

6. Take a day trip to Ephesus 

Tour Details

  • Duration: 6–8 hours
  • Time: Flexible morning departure times
  • Highlights: Exploring ancient Ephesus, seeing the Library of Celsus and Great Theater, optional visits to the House of the Virgin Mary and Temple of Artemis
  • Inclusions: Private licensed guide, air-conditioned Mercedes vehicle and driver, hotel or cruise port pickup and drop-off, parking fees (entrance tickets and lunch extra)
  • Rating: 4.9 stars (check 130+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

If you’ve got a day to spare in Bodrum, we highly recommend booking this private Ephesus day tour. It takes care of all transportation and includes a knowledgeable local guide, making it an easy way to explore one of Turkey’s most impressive ancient cities. Yes, it’s a couple of hours away, but trust us, it’s well worth the journey!

The star of the show is the Library of Celsus, with its enormous, beautifully preserved facade. Honestly, it’s hard to believe this building is almost 2,000 years old! You’ll also see the Great Theater, the Temple of Hadrian, and plenty of other ancient ruins.

Depending on your interests, you can also visit the House of the Virgin Mary, the Terrace Houses, or the remains of the Temple of Artemis, once one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. There’s a LOT of history to get your head around here, so having a guide makes a huge difference.

We also love that the tour is private, so you can spend more time at the places that interest you rather than being rushed around with a big group. The drive takes around 2–2.5 hours each way, so it’s a fairly long day, but you’ll be traveling in a comfortable, air-conditioned vehicle. Trust us, you’ll appreciate that in the Turkish summer! Just remember to budget separately for entrance tickets and lunch, as they’re not included in the tour price.

Book this private Ephesus day tour here and discover one of Turkey’s most incredible ancient cities!

7. Hit the beach

You can’t come to Bodrum without spending some time at the beach! The peninsula has gorgeous stretches of coastline, and plenty of Blue Flag beaches meet high standards for cleanliness and safety.

Now, Bodrum is famous for its swanky beach clubs, but don’t worry if you’re not keen on paying a small fortune for a sunbed. There are plenty of places where you can enjoy the beautiful Aegean Sea without blowing your budget!

Here are three beaches we’d recommend checking out:

  • Yahşi Beach – About 25 minutes from Bodrum town, Yahşi Beach is a popular spot with clear water and a long stretch of sand and pebbles. Plenty of restaurants and beach bars line the shore, so you won’t have to go far when you fancy a cold drink or something to eat.
  • Deve Beach – Also known as Camel Beach, this is a great choice if you’re after soft sand and shallow water. It’s particularly popular with families, and there are lots of sunbeds available to rent. We would happily spend an afternoon here!
  • Bodrum Yalı Çiftlik Public Beach – If you’d prefer somewhere a bit more low-key, head to Yalıçiftlik. It’s surrounded by green hills, the water is beautifully clear, and there’s a public beach where you can lay down your towel without paying beach club prices.

One thing we’d recommend is bringing water shoes, especially if you’re heading to one of the pebbly beaches. And if you’re visiting during July or August, get there early to nab a good spot before everyone else has the same idea!

8. Cruise around the city on a Segway

Tour Details

  • Duration: 2.5 hours
  • Time: 9 am or 1 pm
  • Highlights: Riding a Segway through Bodrum, seeing Bodrum Castle, the Mausoleum, and Myndos Gate, stopping for photos
  • Inclusions: Guided Segway experience, helmet, bottled water, printed photo, small group tour
  • Rating: 5 stars (check 130+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

If you want to explore Bodrum without spending hours traipsing around in the heat, we’ve got a fun alternative for you! This guided Segway tour takes you around the city’s most famous landmarks, and you get to do the whole thing on two wheels.

Never ridden a Segway before? No problem! Your guide will show you how to use one before you set off, so you don’t need any experience. And let’s face it, whizzing around Bodrum on a Segway sounds a lot more fun than walking everywhere.

The tour lasts around 2.5 hours and takes you past up to 20 different landmarks, including Bodrum Castle, the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus, and Myndos Gate. You’ll also explore some quieter streets along the way, which is a great chance to discover parts of Bodrum you might otherwise miss.

There are plenty of photo stops, and your guide will share interesting stories about the city’s history as you go. We love that you get to learn about Bodrum without feeling like you’re back in a history lesson!

The groups are limited to just four people, too, so you won’t be trying to keep up with a huge crowd. And with over 130 five-star reviews (read them here!), it’s clearly a hit. We think this is the perfect thing to do at the start of your trip, as you’ll get your bearings and figure out which spots you want to come back and explore in depth later.

9. Explore Bodrum at your own pace 

Bodrum might be famous for its luxury resorts and glamorous beach clubs, but we think the town itself is just as worth exploring! In fact, some of our favorite things to do here don’t involve booking a tour at all.

Shop and wander through the laneways

Our favorite thing about Bodrum is its maze of narrow streets, with whitewashed buildings adorned with bright pink bougainvillea, and little shops on every corner. Head to the area around Bodrum Bazaar, where you’ll find handmade jewelry, Turkish ceramics, clothes, leather goods, and souvenirs. There are cafés tucked away all over the place too, so you can stop for a Turkish coffee whenever you fancy one. 

Fair warning: you’ll probably end up browsing for way longer than you planned!

Stroll along the marina and waterfront

Bodrum’s waterfront is definitely worth some time too. The marina is full of massive yachts and traditional wooden gulets, with plenty of restaurants and bars overlooking the water.

It’s a lovely place for a late-afternoon wander, once it’s cooled down a bit. 

We actually stayed here until sunset, and it was a good decision because the light over the harbor was just gorgeous. We grabbed a table at Dinc for sunset drinks, then went to Paprika for dinner. We had heard good things about their small plates, and they certainly didn’t disappoint!

10. Relax on a sunset dinner cruise 

Tour Details

  • Duration: 3 hours
  • Time: Evening departure, usually between 5 pm and 6:30 pm depending on sunset
  • Highlights: Private sunset boat cruise, swimming and snorkeling at Aquarium Bay, freshly prepared Turkish dinner, sunset views of Bodrum
  • Inclusions: Private boat and crew, dinner with fish, chicken or vegetarian options, snorkeling equipment, paddleboard, water, soft drinks, tea and coffee (bring your own alcoholic drinks)
  • Rating: 5 stars (check 60+ reviews here)
  • Free Cancellation: Yes
  • Price: Check price here!

We love a sunset cruise at the best of times, but throw in a delicious Turkish dinner and a private boat, and you’ve really got something special! We truly think this three-hour sunset dinner cruise is one of the most special ways to spend an evening in Bodrum.

You’ll set sail from the harbor in the late afternoon and cruise along the beautiful coastline, with incredible views of Bodrum from the water. And since it’s a private tour, you’ll have the entire boat to yourselves.

One highlight is stopping at Aquarium Bay, famous for its clear, beautiful water. You’ll have the chance to swim or snorkel before sitting down for dinner on board.

And what a setting for dinner! You can choose from fish, chicken, or vegetarian options and enjoy your meal as the sun sets over the Aegean.

There’s even snorkeling equipment and a paddleboard available, so you can really make the most of your time in the bay. Or, of course, you can just relax on deck with a drink and enjoy the views. We certainly wouldn’t judge you for that!

We especially love that you can bring your own alcoholic drinks on board, which is handy if you fancy a nice bottle of wine with dinner. We think this would be a fantastic experience for couples, but it would be just as much fun with a group of friends. After all, sunset, dinner, drinks, and sea views are a winning combination for just about everyone!

Where to Stay in Bodrum, Turkey

Bodrum has some incredible luxury resorts, but we think staying in the main town is the best option if you want to explore! You’ll be close to the historic attractions, waterfront restaurants, and plenty of shops, without having to rely on taxis every time you want to go somewhere.

Accommodation in central Bodrum can also be much more affordable than the exclusive resorts dotted around the peninsula. Here are three great hotels to consider, depending on your budget!

The Marmara Bodrum – $$$

If you’re looking for somewhere special, The Marmara Bodrum is an absolutely gorgeous choice! This five-star, adults-only hotel sits on a hillside overlooking Bodrum, and the views are absolutely incredible. You can see right across the city and the Aegean Sea, which is a pretty spectacular backdrop for a vacation.

The hotel has beautiful rooms with elegant furnishings, and many have private balconies or terraces overlooking the water. But our favorite feature has to be the huge outdoor swimming pool, where you can spend your afternoons relaxing with panoramic views of Bodrum. There’s also a spa with a traditional Turkish hammam, a fitness center, and a fantastic restaurant serving Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine.

And if you fancy a day at the beach, the hotel also offers a seasonal shuttle to a partner beach club! As a luxury stay, expect to pay around $200–$480+ USD per night, with rates varying by season and room type. Read the amazing reviews and book your stay at The Marmara Bodrum here!

Su Hotel Bodrum– $$

We absolutely love the look of Su Hotel Bodrum! This charming boutique hotel has a very Cycladic feel, and it’s a little oasis right in the heart of Bodrum.

The rooms are bright and colorful, with traditional Turkish touches, and most overlook the pretty courtyard. There’s an outdoor swimming pool, surrounded by lush greenery and flowering plants, and there’s an on-site restaurant serving delicious Aegean dishes.

Plus, the marina and town center are just a short walk away, so you’ll have plenty of restaurants and shops within easy reach. Nightly rates generally fall somewhere between $130 and $270 USD, making this a lovely mid-range option for a boutique stay in Bodrum. Check availability and book Su Hotel Bodrum here!

Bodrum Sade Otel – $

You don’t have to spend a fortune to stay somewhere charming in Bodrum, and Bodrum Sade Otel definitely proves that! This pretty little boutique hotel is right in the heart of the town, just a short walk from the waterfront and shopping streets.

We love its traditional white-and-blue decor, which feels perfectly suited to Bodrum. The rooms are simple but comfortable, with air conditioning and private bathrooms, and there’s a lovely leafy courtyard to relax in. Breakfast is available, too, and the central location makes it easy to walk to the beach and main attractions without needing a taxi.

You can find rooms for around $50–$160 USD per night, so it’s a great option if you’d rather save your money for exploring Bodrum. Find the best prices and book Bodrum Sade Otel here!
